sammendrag: Norway operates a single, nationwide, generous statutory sickness-absence scheme, whereas the USA has no unified national scheme and instead relies on a fragmented arrangement spanning the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), state and municipal paid-sick-leave laws, and employer- or institution-level benefits. The objective of this scoping review is to map and contrast how sick-leave processes for working-age employed people with musculoskeletal (MSK) disorders operate in Norway versus the USA. Charted domains include eligibility rules, income/wage replacement, follow-up and return-to-work (RTW) regimes, and medical certification processes. A secondary aim is to compare the reported prevalence of MSK-related sickness absence in each country. Charting will permit a structured comparison of Norwegian and USA sick-leave processes across eligibility, income replacement, follow-up/RTW, and certification. Norway is expected to be characterized by a single nationwide system, whereas the USA is expected to present a fragmented structure. Descriptive patterns are anticipated across the primary domains and in the reported prevalence of MSK-related sickness absence. The PRISMA-ScR flow (records identified, screened, and included) and included-source characteristics will be reported. By mapping two structurally divergent systems, this review will describe the extent and nature of available evidence on MSK-related sick-leave processes in Norway and the USA and identify key gaps for future research and policy analysis. The findings are intended to characterize the contrasting approaches: Norway's comprehensive statutory model versus the more restricted and fragmented USA arrangement.
tittel: A Comparison of Norwegian and USA musculoskeletal sick leave processes: A Scoping Review
